About The Job

Head of Engineering

Location:

Seattle, WA, Full-Time

We're hiring a Head of Engineering to reinvent how legal work gets done in the age of AI.

Boundless is a Series C legal tech company based in Seattle, backed by Pioneer Square Labs, Trilogy, Foundry Group (Brad Feld) and Silver Lake. We operate in 10+ countries and have helped over 100,000 people and companies navigate immigration. We build tech-powered immigration solutions for two audiences: corporate HR teams managing high volumes of employer-sponsored cases, and individuals navigating family and naturalization cases.

We have in-house lawyers and are building a world-class AI-powered services firm. Anthropic is not coming for this. Immigration is vertical, regulated, and workflow-deep, and we are racing to build the defining AI product in the category.

Why this role exists

We are rebuilding our software platform and engineering infrastructure from the ground up, and we need a Head of Engineering to lead the team.

You will inherit a real customer base, a real platform, and a great team of engineers.

Immigration is complex, with endless edge cases and global scale. We are building intelligent automation, orchestration, and decision-making to support the agentification of legal workflows, with the checks and balances required to ensure accuracy in a regulated domain and to enable the lawyers who ultimately own legal decisions. The engineering challenge is a team and a system that can handle this complexity without sacrificing accuracy, observability, or speed, at the scale required to reliably serve thousands of people every year.

However, this is not a caretaker role. The world is changing around us and the team is in the midst of transitioning to both an AI-native customer product and an AI-native development process. You will need to drive change with us, and partner with our existing engineering, product, design, legal and operations teams to build a world-class AI-native platform for legal services, and continue to evolve our development infrastructure towards being a truly AI-native “software factory”.

We are looking for someone who can hold the whole picture: the customer, the team, the platform, the AI layer, the delivery system - and how they interact. Someone who makes hard calls, thinks in years not months, and builds an organization that top-tier engineers find exciting and satisfying to be part of.

We are a remote-first team with a small in-person office in Seattle. We want someone based in Seattle and expect you to be in the office a minimum of 2-days per week.

What You Will Do

Build the team. Retain our top performers, hire more top-tier engineers, and lead, inspire, challenge, level, structure, and grow the team.
Own engineering delivery end to end. Roadmap execution, quality, on-call, and the operational health of a platform that customers depend on daily.
Evolve team design as the work changes. Service boundaries and team boundaries move together.
You’ll be a true player-coach: expected to ship code yourself while leading the team and staying close to the details of everything we build.
Drive the AI transition through the team, not around it. Every engineer should be building with LLMs, retrieval, and structured tools as a default.
Build the foundational infrastructure that operating teams use to deploy, monitor, and manage agents and LLM-powered customer features at enormous scale.
Continue our transition towards a “software factory” engineering model, overhauling dev processes, systems, tools, and culture.
Partner with product, design, legal and operations as a peer. Engage thoughtfully in tradeoff conversations about scope, sequencing, and what "done" means in a regulated domain.
Set the technical bar in design reviews and hard tradeoff conversations. Make sure architecture decisions get written down and give the team durable context. Help us build a platform that both engineers and operating teams pine for after they leave.
Grow engineers into architectural thinking by giving them opportunities to step up, and pushing their thinking constructively.

Who You Are

You are a builder. You set new benchmarks for output and want a role where your team ships with autonomy and speed. Not a role where you wait for consensus.
You have 10+ years in engineering and 4+ years managing engineers, including managing managers or senior ICs.
You move fast by making decisions quickly, not by cutting corners. You know the difference between a reversible call and one that will come back to haunt us.
You hire well and manage out when you need to. You have built a team you were proud of and you can describe what made it work.
You have shipped AI into production and led a team through the shift. You have views on retrieval, evaluation, latency, and where LLMs break down, and you know when to use AI and when another tool is the right call.
You have been the technical decision-maker, not just the person who runs the process. You can lead a design review and change the answer.
You think in systems. You can hold the team, the platform, the AI layer, and the business constraints in your head at once and see where they don't line up.
You have taste. You can build teams and systems where agents and humans work in harmony without overbuilding.
You have worked in a domain where correctness has consequences: legal, healthcare, financial services, or public safety. You understand why accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable.

Good Signals, Not Requirements

You have worked at both large and small companies and have a preference for small. You understand speed to impact but also know what matters at scale.
Founder or CTO experience.
You have scaled a team through a platform rebuild or replatforming, and can talk about what you got wrong.
Experience with workflow automation.
Prior work with vector search, semantic retrieval, or document understanding systems at production scale.

jobs.description:

We do not accept unsolicited resumes or sales solicitations from staffing agencies. Any OCC employee wishing to submit a referral must do so through their Workday account. What You'll Do:

The Executive Director, Platform Architecture leads OCC's Platform Architecture team, owning the technical strategy and standards for all infrastructure domains — cloud, onpremises, networking, compute, storage, and observability. This is a people leadership role responsible for developing a team of principal architects and ensuring their work produces coherent, enterprise-wide platform standards rather than isolated domain expertise.

The Executive Director, Platform Architecture translates OCC's resilience objectives and regulatory obligations into actionable platform architecture strategy, drives adoption of that strategy across Engineering and Operations, and ensures the platform layer keeps pace with OCC's technology transformation — including the Renaissance/Ovation program and ongoing cloud adoption.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each primary duty satisfactorily.

Lead the Platform Architecture Team

Lead, develop, and set direction for a team of principal architects covering cloud, on-premises infrastructure, networking, compute, storage, and observability domains
Own the Platform Architecture vision: deliver the resilient, scalable foundation upon which critical market functions depend — making resilience the default, not the exception
Ensure individual architect domain expertise is synthesized into coherent, enterprise-wide platform standards — not siloed recommendations
Manage team priorities, capacity, and delivery against architecture commitments across programs and initiatives Develop team members through coaching, feedback, and exposure to enterprise-scale architectural challenges

Define and Govern Platform Architecture Standards

Establish and maintain authoritative platform architecture standards spanning cloud (AWS), on-premises data center, hybrid connectivity, networking, compute, storage, and container platforms
Define reference architectures and infrastructure patterns that Engineering and application teams can consume without requiring per-project architecture engagement Own non-functional requirements standards at the platform level — availability, fault tolerance, disaster recovery, latency, throughput, and capacity — as first-class concerns applicable across all tiers of OCC's system portfolio
Enforce platform standards through Architecture Review Board participation and design review processes
Maintain infrastructure architecture documentation, ADRs, and transition plans that accurately reflect current and target state

Drive Infrastructure Modernization and Cloud Strategy

Own OCC's infrastructure architecture strategy for cloud adoption — defining what moves to AWS, what remains on-premises, and how hybrid connectivity is structured
Ensure cloud architecture patterns for networking, security, identity, and compute are consistent, compliant, and operationally sound across all workloads Drive GitOps and infrastructure-as-code adoption — pipeline standards, environment promotion, configuration management, and secrets management at enterprise scale
Lead architecture direction for container platform (Kubernetes/EKS), streaming infrastructure (Kafka), and stream processing (Flink) as foundational platform capabilities
Identify and systematically reduce infrastructure risk — single points of failure, end-of-life dependencies, capacity constraints, and gaps in recovery capabilities

Partner Across the Organization

Serve as the primary platform architecture partner to Application Architecture, ensuring application designs are grounded in platform reality and platform capabilities evolve to meet application needs
Collaborate with Engineering, Security, and Operations to ensure platform architecture decisions are implementable, operable, and aligned to security requirements
Engage with Technology Leads, program management, and senior leadership to represent platform architecture in strategic planning, budgeting, and vendor decisions
Coordinate with Governance/Risk and Compliance to ensure platform architecture satisfies OCC's regulatory obligations under Regulation SCI and CPMI-IOSCO resilience principles

Ensure Operational Resilience

Establish observability standards — metrics, logging, distributed tracing, and alerting — as platform-level capabilities delivered to all application teams
Define and govern disaster recovery, business continuity, and resilience architecture across infrastructure domains
Drive capacity planning and performance engineering practices; ensure the platform is sized and architected ahead of demand, not reactive to it
Lead platform architecture participation in incident postmortems; ensure operational findings drive durable infrastructure improvements

Supervisory Responsibilities

Manages a team of principal architects and senior individual contributors across infrastructure architecture domains

Qualifications:

The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the primary functions.

Required

12+ years of experience in infrastructure, platform, or systems architecture, with at least 3 years in a people leadership or team lead role
Demonstrated experience defining and governing infrastructure architecture standards across multiple domains at organizational scale
Broad, hands-on knowledge across infrastructure domains:
cloud (AWS), on-premises data center, networking, compute, storage, and container platforms
Deep experience with AWS architecture — VPCs, EC2, EKS, MSK, S3, IAM, KMS, Direct Connect, Transit Gateway, and security services
Strong working knowledge of Kubernetes — cluster architecture, workload design, multi-tenancy, networking (CNI), and operational patterns at scale
Experience with Apache Kafka as enterprise streaming infrastructure — deployment, operations, and topology design
Demonstrated experience leading GitOps and infrastructure-as-code programs — Terraform, Helm, ArgoCD, Flux, or equivalent
Experience with hybrid and on-premises/cloud connectivity architecture — network design, routing,firewalling, and security zoning
Ability to lead through influence and authority — building alignment across Engineering, Security, Operations, and Governance
Strong communication skills — able to represent infrastructure strategy to executive leadership and translate architecture decisions into actionable standards for engineering teams

Preferred

Experience in financial services, particularly regulated environments (SIFMU, clearinghouse, exchange, or bank)
Familiarity with Regulation SCI, CPMI-IOSCO, or equivalent financial market infrastructure regulatory frameworks and their implications for infrastructure design
Experience with Apache Flink or equivalent stream processing frameworks in production environments
Experience with enterprise observability platforms — OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, or equivalent
Familiarity with low-latency and high-performance computing patterns relevant to risk and clearing workloads AWS Solutions Architect — Professional certification or equivalent
Experience with enterprise architecture frameworks such as TOGAF

EKS, MSK, S3, VPC, IAM, KMS, Direct Connect, Transit Gateway, CloudWatch

Observability: OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, or equivalent

jobs.title: Head of GTM Tools & Technology
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Postman is the world’s leading API platform, used by more than 45 million+ developers and 500,000 organizations, including 98% of the Fortune 500. Postman is helping developers and professionals across the globe build the API-first world by simplifying each step of the API lifecycle and streamlining collaboration—enabling users to create better APIs, faster.

The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Boston, New York, Austin, Tokyo, London, and Bangalore - where Postman was founded. Postman is privately held, with funding from Battery Ventures, BOND, Coatue, CRV, Insight Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. Learn more at postman.com or connect with Postman on X via @getpostman.

P.S: We highly recommend reading The "API-First World" graphic novel to understand the bigger picture and our vision at Postman.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Senior Director/Director, GTM Tools & Technology to own the systems and tooling that power Postman's entire go-to-market organization. This is a strategic leadership role sitting at the intersection of business operations, systems architecture, and AI innovation.

You'll be the internal product owner for our GTM tech stack — from Salesforce at its core, to every platform that plugs into it, across both pre-sale and post-sale. You'll define the vision and drive the roadmap for how we use technology and AI to make our GTM teams faster, smarter, and more effective. This role demands both strategic range and operational depth: you'll partner directly with GTM executives across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Professional Services, Revenue Operations, and Finance, while leading a team to deliver on a high bar.

The standard we're hiring to is high. We want someone who can architect for where Postman is going, not just maintain what exists — and who will lead meaningfully on AI adoption as a first-class mandate.

What You’ll Do

GTM Systems Strategy & Roadmap

Define and execute the roadmap for Postman's GTM tech stack across the full customer lifecycle — from pipeline to renewal and expansion.
Translate business needs from Sales, CS, Professional Services, and GTM Ops into scalable system solutions, balancing build vs. buy decisions with long-term architectural coherence.
Serve as the primary business systems partner and trusted advisor to GTM leadership — surfacing opportunities, managing tradeoffs, and aligning stakeholders on priorities.
Own the GTM tools budget; drive ROI accountability across the portfolio and manage vendor relationships, contracts, and renewals.
Collaborate closely with Marketing Ops on the overall GTM platform strategy and AI roadmap, ensuring alignment across the full funnel without duplicating ownership.

AI Roadmap for GTM

Drive the AI roadmap for the GTM organization in close collaboration with GTM leadership, Engineering, and Operations.
Identify the highest-impact opportunities to embed AI and automation across the revenue lifecycle: lead scoring, pipeline forecasting, conversation intelligence, rep productivity, automated enrichment, next-best-action, and customer health signals.
Partner with IT, Data Engineering, and Analytics to build the data foundation required for reliable AI outputs — clean, unified, and governed.
Establish a repeatable framework for assessing, piloting, and scaling AI tools within the GTM stack, including change management and adoption measurement.
Represent the GTM org's AI priorities in cross-functional conversations with executive leadership and Engineering.

Pre-Sale Systems

Own the design, configuration, governance, and continuous improvement of Salesforce Sales Cloud as the system of record for the GTM org.
Manage integrations across the pre-sale stack (e.g., Outreach/Salesloft, Clari, ZoomInfo, CPQ, Docusign, Ironclad, etc.) ensuring data flows are reliable, clean, and auditable.
Lead system-level support for major GTM initiatives including territory changes, compensation plan rollouts, new product launches, and go-to-market model shifts.

Post-Sale Ecosystem

Own the systems architecture for Postman's post-sale teams, including Professional Services Automation (Rocketlane, Certinia, or equivalent), customer service and ticketing (Zendesk, Intercom, Service Cloud, or equivalent), and Customer Success platforms (Gainsight, Catalyst, or equivalent).
Ensure post-sale systems are well-integrated with Salesforce and the broader GTM data model, enabling a unified view of the customer lifecycle.
Partner with CS, Professional Services, and Support leadership to continuously improve workflows, automation, and data quality across post-sale tools.

Process & Workflow Automation

Identify and eliminate manual, error-prone processes across the lead-to-cash and post-sale lifecycle through automation, smarter tooling, and process redesign.
Champion a low-code/no-code approach to operational efficiency, while knowing when to engage Engineering for more complex builds.
Own documentation, change management, and communication for all system changes affecting the GTM org.

Team Leadership

Lead and develop a team of systems professionals; set direction, grow talent, and build organizational capacity.
Foster a culture of rigor, ownership, and continuous improvement within the team.
Hire and structure the team as Postman's GTM systems needs evolve.

About You

Essential Qualifications

10+ years in business systems, revenue operations technology, or GTM systems roles at high-growth B2B SaaS companies.
Deep hands-on Salesforce expertise (Sales Cloud); Salesforce Admin certification or equivalent practical depth required.
Demonstrated experience owning a GTM tech stack end-to-end — strategy through execution — across both pre-sale and post-sale systems.
Track record of building and delivering multi-year systems roadmaps with measurable business impact.
Experience evaluating and deploying AI and automation tools in a GTM or revenue context.
Proven ability to partner with Engineering as a co-stakeholder on systems and AI initiatives.
Experience managing and developing a team of admins, analysts, and developers.
Strong executive communication skills — you can translate technical complexity for a CRO and business requirements for an engineering team.

Bonus Qualifications

Salesforce Architect certification (Application Architect, System Architect, or CTA).
Experience with iPaaS / integration tools (Workato, MuleSoft, Boomi, or equivalent).
Prior experience at a developer-focused or PLG (product-led growth) SaaS company.
Exposure to revenue recognition or finance systems (Zuora, Stripe Billing, NetSuite, or equivalent).
Experience driving systems roadmaps for M&A integration.

Technical Familiarity

CRM: Salesforce Sales Cloud (SOQL, Flow, reports/dashboards)
CPQ: Salesforce CPQ, DealHub, or equivalent).
Sales Engagement: Outreach, Salesloft, or equivalent
Revenue Intelligence: Clari, Gong, or equivalent
Data Enrichment: ZoomInfo, Clearbit, or equivalent
Post-Sale / PSA: Rocketlane, Certinia, or equivalent
Customer Success: Gainsight, Catalyst, or equivalent
Customer Service: Zendesk, Intercom, Service Cloud, or equivalent
BI / Analytics: Tableau, Looker, or equivalent
Marketing Automation (collaboration, not ownership): Marketo, HubSpot, or equivalent

The reasonably estimated base salary for this role ranges from $230,000 to $290,000, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is based on the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience.

What Else?

In addition to Postman's pay-on-performance philosophy, and a flexible schedule working with a fun, collaborative team, Postman offers a comprehensive set of benefits, including full medical coverage, flexible PTO, wellness reimbursement, and a monthly lunch stipend. Along with that, our wellness programs will help you stay in the best of your physical and mental health. Our frequent and fascinating team-building events will keep you connected, while our donation-matching program can support the causes you care about. We’re building a long-term company with an inclusive culture where everyone can be the best version of themselves.

At Postman we value in person collaboration. We are in office 5 days a week for all roles based out of our hubs in San Francisco Bay Area, Boston, Austin, New York City, Tokyo and London. For roles based in Bangalore, employees currently work in the office three days a week and will transition to five days per week by the end of the year. We were thoughtful in our approach which is based on collaboration and grounded in feedback from our workforce, leadership team, and peers. The benefits of our in office model will be shared knowledge, brainstorming sessions, communication, and building trust in-person that cannot be replicated via zoom.

Our Values

At Postman, we create with the same curiosity that we see in our users. We value transparency and honest communication about not only successes, but also failures. In our work, we focus on specific goals that add up to a larger vision. Our inclusive work culture ensures that everyone is valued equally as important pieces of our final product. We are dedicated to delivering the best products we can.

Equal opportunity

Postman is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. Headhunters and recruitment agencies may not submit resumes/CVs through this website or directly to managers. Postman does not accept unsolicited headhunter and agency resumes. Postman will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with Postman.

About The Job

Head of Engineering

We're hiring a Head of Engineering to reinvent how legal work gets done in the age of AI.

Boundless is a Series C legal tech company based in Seattle, backed by Pioneer Square Labs, Trilogy, Foundry Group (Brad Feld) and Silver Lake. We operate in 10+ countries and have helped over 100,000 people and companies navigate immigration. We build tech-powered immigration solutions for two audiences: corporate HR teams managing high volumes of employer-sponsored cases, and individuals navigating family and naturalization cases.

We have in-house lawyers and are building a world-class AI-powered services firm. Anthropic is not coming for this. Immigration is vertical, regulated, and workflow-deep, and we are racing to build the defining AI product in the category.

Why this role exists

We are rebuilding our software platform and engineering infrastructure from the ground up, and we need a Head of Engineering to lead the team.

You will inherit a real customer base, a real platform, and a great team of engineers.

Immigration is complex, with endless edge cases and global scale. We are building intelligent automation, orchestration, and decision-making to support the agentification of legal workflows, with the checks and balances required to ensure accuracy in a regulated domain and to enable the lawyers who ultimately own legal decisions. The engineering challenge is a team and a system that can handle this complexity without sacrificing accuracy, observability, or speed, at the scale required to reliably serve thousands of people every year.

However, this is not a caretaker role. The world is changing around us and the team is in the midst of transitioning to both an AI-native customer product and an AI-native development process. You will need to drive change with us, and partner with our existing engineering, product, design, legal and operations teams to build a world-class AI-native platform for legal services, and continue to evolve our development infrastructure towards being a truly AI-native “software factory”.

We are looking for someone who can hold the whole picture: the customer, the team, the platform, the AI layer, the delivery system - and how they interact. Someone who makes hard calls, thinks in years not months, and builds an organization that top-tier engineers find exciting and satisfying to be part of.

We are a remote-first team with a small in-person office in Seattle. We want someone based in Seattle and expect you to be in the office a minimum of 2-days per week.

What You Will Do

Build the team. Retain our top performers, hire more top-tier engineers, and lead, inspire, challenge, level, structure, and grow the team.
Own engineering delivery end to end. Roadmap execution, quality, on-call, and the operational health of a platform that customers depend on daily.
Evolve team design as the work changes. Service boundaries and team boundaries move together.
You’ll be a true player-coach: expected to ship code yourself while leading the team and staying close to the details of everything we build.
Drive the AI transition through the team, not around it. Every engineer should be building with LLMs, retrieval, and structured tools as a default.
Build the foundational infrastructure that operating teams use to deploy, monitor, and manage agents and LLM-powered customer features at enormous scale.
Continue our transition towards a “software factory” engineering model, overhauling dev processes, systems, tools, and culture.
Partner with product, design, legal and operations as a peer. Engage thoughtfully in tradeoff conversations about scope, sequencing, and what "done" means in a regulated domain.
Set the technical bar in design reviews and hard tradeoff conversations. Make sure architecture decisions get written down and give the team durable context. Help us build a platform that both engineers and operating teams pine for after they leave.
